props.title: How to Train Your Dragon
props.initialSlug: A boy befriends a feared dragon, changing his world

sections.content: How to Train Your Dragon revolutionized DreamWorks Animation's approach to emotional storytelling. While previous hits like Shrek (2001) relied heavily on pop culture jokes, Dragon crafted a genuine coming-of-age story about acceptance and challenging prejudice. The film's technical achievements, particularly in flying sequences that rival Avatar (2009) for sheer cinematic spectacle, set new standards for animated aerial photography. Directors Chris Sanders and Dean DeBlois, fresh from Disney's Lilo & Stitch (2002), brought their signature blend of creature design and heartfelt character relationships.

sections.content: The film's success sparked a renaissance in animated dragon features. Dragon influenced everything from Raya and the Last Dragon (2021) to Onward (2020), proving audiences would embrace complex themes in family films. The relationship between Hiccup and Toothless redefined human-creature bonds in animation, moving beyond simple pet dynamics into something more nuanced and equal. This partnership echoes through later works like The Good Dinosaur (2015) and Big Hero 6 (2014).

The Viking setting broke new ground for American animation, which had largely stuck to fairy tales or contemporary settings. Its success paved the way for more culturally specific stories like Brave (2012) and Moana (2016). The film's sound design, particularly in Toothless's vocalizations, created by combining various animal sounds, influenced creature sound work in both animation and live action, including Pacific Rim (2013) and The Last Guardian (2016). movies.title: Kubo and the Two Strings
movies.slug: Laika's stunning stop-motion adventure featuring magical creatures and powerful themes about family and storytelling

sections.content: The film's visual style, particularly its use of Roger Deakins as cinematographic consultant, changed how animated films approach lighting and camera movement. This influence is evident in films like The Bad Guys (2022) and Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022), which push animation beyond traditional "safe" visual choices. The success of Dragon's dramatic moments, particularly Hiccup's loss of his leg, showed that family animation could handle serious consequences, influencing films like Into the Spider-Verse (2018) and Wolfwalkers (2020).
